name: Cross-method reproducibility of electronic-structure observables (Delta-gauge)
conventions: each method's energy is referenced to its own minimum before differencing — absolute total energies are basis-dependent and not comparable
spreads are max-min across all methods compared, not pairwise
the compared runs must share atoms, XC functional and pseudopotential; otherwise the spread measures differing inputs, not differing methods
Delta is reported per atom so cells of different size can be compared
expectedLimits: Delta -> 0 as both methods approach basis-set completeness
agreement is evidence of consistency, never of correctness — two methods sharing an approximation can agree and both be wrong
the bulk modulus is far more basis-sensitive than the lattice constant, so it is compared and reported but does not gate the verdict
a comparison of fewer than two methods is not a reproducibility result and must not report agreement
references: Lejaeghere et al. 2014, Crit. Rev. Solid State Mater. Sci. 39, 1
Bosoni et al. 2024, Nat. Rev. Phys. 6, 45

latticeConstant_A.basis: the scale at which independent all-electron and pseudopotential codes are held to agree in the Delta-gauge reproducibility studies

indirectGap_eV.basis: loose band-structure tolerance; gaps are sensitive to k-sampling and basis completeness before any method difference enters

bulkModulus_GPa.basis: reported for information only — B_0 depends on curvature and is dominated by basis quality, so a divergence here diagnoses a method rather than invalidating the comparison
